Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — Recap & next steps

Hi Emily,

Great to speak with you today 











— thanks for walking through your realtime chat use case. Quick recap from my side and a suggested set of next steps so we can get you a concrete recommendation: 

Summary of needs (from call)
- Single-turn chat latency target: 95th percentile <= 120ms
- Peak throughput: ~700-900 req/s (bursty daytime traffic)
- Requests include short context (~150 tokens) + user prompt
- Data sensitivity: some PII (customer names, emails) — must satisfy our standard data isolation options

Initial assessment
- Hosted API can be a great fit if your latency SLO is relaxed or your avg qps is modest.
- Given the 95p <=120ms and sustained peak ~800 req/s, Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) is worth evaluating — it gives predictable p99/95 latency and avoids noisy-neighbor variability.

Proposed next steps
1) Can you confirm the 95p latency target and whether 120ms is a hard requirement?
2) Share a short sample of traffic distribution (RPS over time) or a 24h histogram — even a CSV is fine.
3) If 120ms is firm, I’ll loop in Neha (infra) and Marissa (solutions) to propose a Dedicated configuration and a quick POC plan.

If it helps, we can also run a quick hosted pilot to baseline latency before sizing Dedicated. Let me know what you prefer.

Thanks,
Dylan

Thanks Dylan — good recap. A couple clarifications: 

- The 120ms 95th is more of a hard goal for our customer SLA; if we can be consistently under that we’re happy.
- Peak is often bursty: baseline ~200 qps, spikes up to 800–900 qps for 60–90s windows during promotions.
- Payloads are small (100–300 tokens total).
- We cannot send raw PII to multi-tenant systems without contractual language — so data isolation options matter.

I’ll put together a short CSV of our hour-by-hour RPS for the last 7 days and share it by EOD tomorrow.

If you think Dedicated is the right call, we’re open to evaluating a reserved pool + burst capacity. What would a POC look like from your side?

Hi Emily — thanks for the traffic CSV, and thanks Dylan for the heads-up. Quick recommendation after looking at the distribution and the burst profile:

Recommendation
- Run a 72-hour POC using Dedicated Reserved Pool (suggested starting config: 4x A100-class GPUs equivalent with autoscaling and burst capacity). This gives predictable 95/99 latency and headroom for the 60–90s spikes.
- Configure aggressive prefix KV caching + request-level batching tuned for short-context chat to keep token-level CPU/GPU work minimal.
- Data isolation: Dedicated gives tenant-level isolation; include a clause for no-log retention for sensitive fields and an option for Private VPC if legal requires it.

POC plan
1) Day 0: Provision dedicated pool + sample load generator config (we’ll send the test harness).
2) Day 1–3: Run baseline hosted test (hourly windows) then Dedicated test (same traffic) — collect 95/99 latency and cost metrics.
3) Day 4: Review results + decision meeting (30m).

Attachment: proposed-dedicated-config.pdf (high-level sizing & autoscale rules).

If that works, Dylan — can you confirm we have Emily’s permission to schedule the provisioning window and share cloud credentials (temporary) for the POC infra? Emily — happy to brief your security team on what isolation covers.

Thanks,
